Deck import → mechanics: coverage matrix

Frozen sources preserved. Direct labels tested against actual card data. Updated October 17, 2026. Acquisition uses public Scryfall endpoints; audit and report generation are offline, deterministic and use no model calls or probabilistic matching.

Every named source entry has a row: 524 master entries + 216 color-pie entries. Three playtest category pointers are retained separately. Overlapping categories and source identities are deliberately not merged. The contract supplies constraints, not additional mechanics.

SourceDirect*RulesReview / exceptionsCategory pointers
Master inventory2961121163
Color-pie runtime19180170

*Direct is a bounded claim: exact provider-reported keyword membership permits a neutral label display. It does not establish inherent possession, a particular face, parameters, every grant or every occurrence. Only 8 unique mechanics are currently enabled by the application's reviewed crosswalk; this audit does not expand application support. Source overlap remains in these row counts.

Actual Scryfall validation

296 of 312 distinct candidate labels observed across 38,753 Oracle card records: 288 beyond the original eight. 293 occur on at least one paper, Commander-legal record. Snapshot: 2026-10-17T09:01:58.799+00:00. All three catalogs and raw card data are retained with SHA-256 hashes.

16 direct candidates failed: Abandon, Absorb, Best in show, Descend 4, Descend 8, Face a Villainous Choice, Gear up, Gotcha!, Harness, Planeswalk, Poisonous, Set in Motion, Space Sculptor, The Ring Tempts You, Visit, Vote. Their rows now require rules or scoped review. This does not mean those mechanics do not exist.

Catalog disagreements: Parade! (absent from catalogs); Plot (keyword-actions); Start Your Engines! (ability-words). We preserve both sources and do not silently rewrite the inventory classification.

Verification: 312 indexed results cross-checked by a separate full scan; 13 real-card adversarial cases; 39 mutation checks. 305 witness cards fetched again through the live collection endpoint; 0 compared-field mismatches. This is same-provider consistency, not independent rules verification.

Full validation results · Raw acquisition manifest and hashes · Live witness-check receipts

  • Rules: reusable, explicit text/field parsers; preserve conditions and reject unsupported forms. The matrix specifies them but does not implement them.
  • Review / exceptions: define editorial labels, aliases or special domains first. Some will become reusable rules; unusual cards may need versioned ID exceptions. No claim that each needs manual card mapping.
  • Verification boundary: exact metadata occurrence is measured. Semantic precision/recall and complete mechanic coverage remain unmeasured.

Reproduce the retained-data audit without network access: node scripts/audit-mechanics-metadata.mjs --check. Then verify the matrix: node scripts/build-mechanics-coverage.mjs --check. The raw snapshots are immutable; acquisition scripts refuse to overwrite them.

What to build from this

Keep source identities and dated color information intact. Add a separate provider-label crosswalk, bounded rule recognizers, and explicit exception records. Compile against a pinned card snapshot. Import-time work becomes card-ID lookup, deduplication and fixed displays. Every match must retain rule ID, data revision, source field/excerpt and face when established.

First implement neutral reported-keyword displays and validate provider aliases. Next validate bounded effects such as token creation, counters, zone movement and sacrifice cost/effect distinctions. Keep unresolved definitions disabled. Missing evidence is unknown, not evidence of absence. No strategic inference, combination inference or color-based detection is included.

Complete machine-readable matrix · Deterministic generator and classification policy. Rebuild: node scripts/build-mechanics-coverage.mjs. Check without writing: node scripts/build-mechanics-coverage.mjs --check.

Preserved keyword variant notes (23)
  • **Landwalk**: islandwalk, swampwalk, mountainwalk, plainswalk, forestwalk, nonbasic landwalk, artifact landwalk, snow landwalk, etc. Master source line 230
  • **Protection**: protection from colors, multicolor, named cards, card types, subtypes, and other characteristics. Master source line 231
  • **Cycling**: basic typecycling and other typecycling variants. Master source line 232
  • **Devour**: devour [type] variants. Master source line 233
  • **Equip**: equip [quality] and equip planeswalker variants. Master source line 234
  • **Hexproof**: hexproof from [quality] variants. Master source line 235
  • **Trample**: trample over planeswalkers variant. Master source line 236
  • **Partner**: Partner with [name], Choose a Background, and Doctor's companion variants. Master source line 237
  • **Ninjutsu**: Commander ninjutsu variant. Master source line 238
  • **Morph**: Megamorph variant. Master source line 239
  • **Hidden Agenda**: Double agenda variant. Master source line 240
  • **Ascend**: includes the City's blessing state. Master source line 241
  • **Visit**: includes Prize variants. Master source line 242
  • **Storied**: includes Enduring story variants. Master source line 243
  • **Web-slinging**: includes Enweb variants. Master source line 244
  • **Start Your Engines!**: includes the Speed / Max speed framework. Master source line 245
  • **Manifest** includes Manifest Dread. Master source line 324
  • **Venture into the Dungeon** includes Venture into [quality]. Master source line 325
  • **Tap and Untap** is one CR entry covering both actions. Master source line 326
  • **Open an Attraction** and **Roll to Visit Your Attractions** belong to the Attraction framework. Master source line 327
  • **The Ring Tempts You** and **Face a Villainous Choice** are multiword keyword actions. Master source line 328
  • **Airbend**, **Earthbend**, and **Waterbend** are Universes Beyond-specific. Master source line 329
  • **Empower Jace** is a highly specific, set-specific action. Master source line 330

                                                                                                          • Mishra's Manufactory // Mishra's Manufactory (cont'd)keywords: []Oracle ID: 55a3c992-12b1-4025-8060-8b28991539fcMishra's Manufactory: 2-4 players | 2-4 packs | 10 min OBJECTIVE: Take on the role of one of Mishra's assembly workers and assemble the best invention from the mishmash of parts streaming down the conveyor belt. Strategically collect cards based on their color to win. GET READY: Open one booster for each player, remove all cards without _Magic_ card backs, and shuffle the rest together. Reveal four cards in a row stretching from the deck. These form the *conveyor belt*. The two cards closest to the deck are at the *back of the line* and the other two cards are at the *front*. Randomly determine who goes first. LET'S PLAY: On their turn, each player drafts one card from the conveyor belt. The two cards at the front of the line are free, but a player must discard a card they've already collected to draft a card from the back of the Mishra's Manufactory (cont'd): line. Cards then slide forward to fill in the gap, and a card from the deck is added to the back of the line. Drafted cards are kept face up in front of each player, grouped by color (including colorless.) Play then passes clockwise. Lands are wild (they count as any color, including colorless), and a multicolored card can be any of its colors. When you draft a wild or multicolored card, declare its color and place it in the corresponding group. TO WIN: The game ends when all cards have been collected. For each color, the player with the largest group of cards of that color gets *3 points*, and the player with the second largest group gets *2 points*. The card with the highest mana value breaks ties. If there is still a tie, each tied player gets half the points, rounded up. Players also earn points for the number of groups they've collected: four groups = *2 points*, five groups = *4 points*, six groups = *6 points*. The player with the most points wins!

Race your fellow artificers to assemble all three iconic locations. GET READY: Open a booster for each player and remove any cards without _Magic_ card backs. Shuffle the remaining cards into a deck and deal five cards to each player. Randomly determine who goes first. LET'S PLAY: On each player's turn, they draw a card, then discard a card face up. Players may draw either the top card of the deck or the top card of the discard pile. If there are no cards left in the deck when a player tries to draw, shuffle the discard pile to form a new deck. Urza's Blueprints (cont'd): After discarding, if a player has all the cards required for a new location (see below), they may reveal those cards and note they have constructed their version of that location. They must then discard all cards in their hand and draw a new hand of five cards. Play then passes to the next player. Foils are wild and can cont as any color, mana value, or card type. TO WIN: The first player to construct all three locations wins! THE LOCATIONS: *Mine:* Requires five cards with different card types. (Creature, artifact, land, etc.) *Power Plant:* Requires one card of each color. (White, blue, black, red, and green. Multicolored cards count as one color of your choice. Lands are colorless.) *Tower:* Requires five cards with different mana values. (Lands have mana value 0.)

                                                                                                                          • Booster Sleuth // Booster Sleuth (cont'd)keywords: []Oracle ID: 17df4eab-fd77-49bf-bad4-018516931b3eBooster Sleuth: 2 players | 2 packs | 10 minutes OBJECTIVE: Unlike Jace, not all of us can rely on telepathy to solve a mystery. Using other cards as clues, discover all the facts about your opponent's mystery card. GET READY: Randomly determine who goes first—that player is the Secretkeeper, and their opponent is the Detective. First, the Secretkeeper opens a pack and removes any lands and cards without Magic card backs. Next, they shuffle the remaining cards and pick one at random. That card is the mystery card. Finally, the Secretkeeper gives the Detective the rest of the cards, and the game begins. LET'S PLAY: The Detective must correctly guess four facts Booster Sleuth (cont'd): about the mystery card: converted mana cost, color, card type, and the number of words in its name. To do this, they choose and reveal cards one at a time. When each card is revealed, the Secretkeeper tells the Detective how many of the four facts that card and the mystery card have in common. Then the Detective may either guess the four facts or reveal another card to get more clues. The Detective gets only one guess, and they must guess all four facts correctly to win. Once the Detective has guessed, the round ends and the players switch roles with a new pack. TO WIN: Discover all four facts using as few cards as possible. The Detective who guesses correctly using the fewest clue cards wins! If neither player guessed correctly, or if there is a tie, play another round!
